name: Goods and their vessels
_about: WHAT EACH CULTURE SHIPS ITS GOODS IN (2026-11-03; freight.js, carts.js, index.html; docs/world.md 'Freight'). `cultures`: keyed by the world's period (periods.json, PERIOD_NAME), else by the first style of the period's `dress`, else `default`. Each gives `freight` -- the vessels of the barge-to-yard chain (the dock hands' loads, the freight carts' beds, the yards) as {vessel: weight}: the pool of `pool` pieces is shared out by weight; `carry` -- per vessel, how a porter carries it (a style of `carry` below; the vessel's own `carry` if not said); `loads` -- the road carts' load variants (items/components/cart-*: 0 casks lying, 1 standing casks, 2 kegs, 3 sacks, 4 casks and sacks, 6 amphorae in straw, 7 amphorae and sacks, 8 jars and hampers in straw, 9 bales, 10 crates and sacks, 11 tubs and bales, 12 rice bales); `teams` -- the draught beasts it put to carts (absent: all; [] none, so no carts: the Maya had no draught animals; Egypt and Japan oxen); `store` -- a vessel kept in the freight yards' stores (Greek pithoi), `n` of them. `vessels`: the item, its params, how it lies when set down (`rest`: `rot` degrees x y z, `at` metres, in its own frame -- an amphora on its belly, a sack across), its `carry` style and where it sits in that style's frame (`carried`: at, rot). `carry`: the porter's styles -- the figure's `pose` (people.js), the anchor (`from`: the feet, the top of the shoulder or the crown of the head, read off the figure; +x its forward, +z its right) and `at` from it; `with`: an item carried along (the carrying pole, the tumpline strap). Sources: transport amphorae lying in straw on carts and in holds and carried on the shoulder (Attic vase painting, Roman reliefs -- the Ostia and Igel reliefs show casks only north of the Alps from the 1st century); pithoi as storage (Knossos magazines); Egyptian porters with jars and baskets on the head and the shoulder (tomb paintings, Ti, Rekhmire); Chinese and Japanese carrying poles (biandan, tenbin-bo) with tubs and baskets, Japanese rice in straw tawara; Ottoman hamals with bales on the back; Maya porters with the tumpline (mecapal); medieval and later Europe casks, sacks and crates.

arms._about: held in both arms before the belly

shoulder._about: on the right shoulder, the right hand up steadying it

head._about: on the head on a pad, the right hand up at its side

pole._about: hung from the front of a pole on the right shoulder, the porter's own basket behind, the right hand on the pole before him

back._about: on the back, high, the hands at the cords over the shoulders

tumpline._about: on the back, held by the strap over the forehead, the hands up at the strap
